column2:
hacker(n.)駭客
hack(v.)入侵(電腦系統)
hacking(n.)駭客行為
computer hacker 電腦駭客
hacker attack 駭客攻擊
A hacker broke into the company's system and stole customer data.
(一名駭客入侵公司的系統並竊取了客戶資料。)
The bank hired experts to protect its website from hacker attacks.
(那家銀行聘請專家保護網站免受駭客攻擊。)

hail(n./v.)冰雹、下冰雹、歡呼、招呼
(無詞性變化)
hail a taxi 招計程車
be hailed as 被譽為
Heavy hail damaged many cars parked along the street last night.
(昨晚的大冰雹損壞了許多停在路邊的車。)
The young scientist was hailed as a hero after her discovery.
(那位年輕科學家在有所發現後被譽為英雄。)

hamper(v.)妨礙、阻礙
(無詞性變化)
hamper efforts 阻礙努力
hamper progress 妨礙進展
Heavy rain hampered the rescue workers' efforts to reach the village.
(大雨妨礙了救難人員抵達村莊的行動。)
A lack of funding has seriously hampered the progress of the research.
(資金短缺嚴重阻礙了研究的進展。)

handicap(n./v.)障礙、不利條件、妨礙
handicapped(adj.)身心障礙的
physical handicap 身體障礙
be handicapped by 受…所阻礙
Not speaking the local language can be a real handicap when traveling.
(旅行時不會說當地語言可能是很大的不利條件。)
The team was handicapped by injuries to two key players.
(球隊因兩名主力球員受傷而處於劣勢。)

handicraft(n.)手工藝、手工藝品
(無詞性變化)
traditional handicrafts 傳統手工藝品
handicraft market 手工藝市集
Tourists often buy traditional handicrafts as souvenirs in Lukang.
(遊客在鹿港常會買傳統手工藝品當作紀念品。)
The village is famous for its bamboo handicrafts made by local artists.
(這個村莊以當地藝術家製作的竹編手工藝品聞名。)

harass(v.)騷擾、侵擾、harassment(n.)騷擾
(無詞性變化)
sexual harassment 性騷擾
online harassment 網路騷擾
The singer complained that photographers kept harassing her family.
(那位歌手抱怨攝影師一直騷擾她的家人。)
The school has clear rules to deal with online harassment among students.
(學校有明確的規定來處理學生之間的網路騷擾。)

harden(v.)使變硬、變得冷酷、使堅定
hard(adj.)硬的
hardened(adj.)變硬的、冷酷無情的
harden one's heart 硬起心腸
harden into 變硬成為
The melted chocolate will harden as it cools down.
(融化的巧克力冷卻後會變硬。)
Years of hardship had hardened him into a cold and silent man.
(多年的艱苦使他變成一個冷漠寡言的人。)

harmonica(n.)口琴
(無詞性變化)
play the harmonica 吹口琴
harmonica band 口琴隊
My grandfather taught me how to play the harmonica when I was ten.
(我十歲時，爺爺教我吹口琴。)
She joined the school harmonica band and practiced every afternoon.
(她加入學校的口琴隊，每天下午都練習。)

harness(n./v.)馬具、安全吊帶、駕馭、利用
(無詞性變化)
harness energy 利用能源
safety harness 安全吊帶
Many countries are trying to harness wind and solar energy.
(許多國家正努力利用風能與太陽能。)
Climbers must wear a safety harness at all times.
(攀岩者必須全程穿戴安全吊帶。)

haunt(v./n.)(鬼魂)出沒、縈繞心頭、常去的地方
haunted(adj.)鬧鬼的
haunting(adj.)縈繞心頭的
haunted house 鬼屋
favorite haunt 常去的地方
People say the old house on the hill is haunted by a ghost.
(人們說山丘上那棟老房子有鬼出沒。)
The memory of the accident continued to haunt him for years.
(那場意外的記憶多年來一直縈繞在他心頭。)

headphone(n.)耳機、headphones(n.)頭戴式耳機
(無詞性變化)
wear headphones 戴耳機
noise-canceling headphones 降噪耳機
He always wears headphones on the MRT to avoid the noise.
(他搭捷運時總是戴著耳機以隔絕噪音。)
Listening to loud music through headphones can damage your hearing.
(用耳機聽很大聲的音樂可能會損害聽力。)

healthful(adj.)有益健康的
health(n.)健康
healthy(adj.)健康的
healthful diet 有益健康的飲食
healthful food 健康食品
A healthful diet should include plenty of fresh fruits and vegetables.
(有益健康的飲食應該包含大量新鮮蔬果。)
Walking in fresh air is a simple and healthful habit.
(在新鮮空氣中散步是簡單又有益健康的習慣。)

hearty(adj.)熱忱的、豐盛的、衷心的
heartily(adv.)熱情地、盡情地
hearty meal 豐盛的一餐
hearty welcome 熱烈的歡迎
After the long hike, we enjoyed a hearty meal at a local restaurant.
(長途健行後，我們在當地餐廳享用了一頓豐盛的餐點。)
The exchange students received a hearty welcome from their host families.
(交換學生受到寄宿家庭熱烈的歡迎。)

hedge(n./v.)樹籬、防範措施、避免正面回答
(無詞性變化)
hedge against 防範、對沖
trim the hedge 修剪樹籬
My father spent the whole afternoon trimming the hedge in the garden.
(我爸爸花了整個下午修剪花園裡的樹籬。)
When reporters asked about the scandal, the minister hedged and changed the subject.
(記者詢問醜聞時，部長避重就輕並轉移話題。)

heighten(v.)提高、增強、加劇
height(n.)高度
heightened(adj.)提高的
heighten awareness 提高意識
heighten tension 加劇緊張
The campaign aims to heighten public awareness of ocean pollution.
(這項活動旨在提高大眾對海洋汙染的意識。)
The dramatic music heightened the tension in the final scene of the movie.
(戲劇性的配樂增強了電影最後一幕的緊張感。)

hemisphere(n.)半球、大腦半球
(無詞性變化)
Northern Hemisphere 北半球
left hemisphere 左腦
When it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere, it is winter in Australia.
(北半球是夏天時，澳洲正值冬天。)
The left hemisphere of the brain is closely linked to language.
(大腦的左半球與語言能力密切相關。)

heroic(adj./n.)英勇的、英雄的、英雄式的言行
hero(n.)英雄
heroism(n.)英勇行為
heroic act 英勇的行為
heroic effort 英勇的努力
The firefighter received a medal for his heroic act during the fire.
(那位消防員因在火災中的英勇行為而獲頒獎章。)
Despite their heroic efforts, the doctors could not save the patient.
(儘管醫生們盡了最大努力，仍未能救回那名病人。)

heroin(n.)海洛因
(無詞性變化)
heroin addiction 海洛因成癮
heroin smuggling 海洛因走私
Customs officers found a large amount of heroin hidden in the suitcase.
(海關人員在行李箱中發現大量藏匿的海洛因。)
The documentary shows how heroin addiction can destroy a family.
(這部紀錄片呈現海洛因成癮如何摧毀一個家庭。)

heterosexual(adj./n.)異性戀的、異性戀者
heterosexuality(n.)異性戀
heterosexual couple 異性伴侶
heterosexual relationship 異性關係
The survey included both heterosexual and same-sex couples.
(這項調查同時涵蓋了異性伴侶與同性伴侶。)
The law gives same-sex couples the same rights as heterosexual couples.
(這項法律賦予同性伴侶與異性伴侶相同的權利。)

hierarchy(n.)階級制度、等級體系
hierarchical(adj.)階級制的
social hierarchy 社會階級
in the hierarchy 在階級體系中
In the past, the social hierarchy decided what jobs people could have.
(在過去，社會階級決定了人們能從事什麼工作。)
She quickly moved up the company's hierarchy because of her ability.
(她憑藉能力在公司的階級體系中迅速晉升。)

hijack(v./n.)劫持(交通工具)、挾持、劫機事件
hijacker(n.)劫機者
hijack a plane 劫機
hijack a conversation 搶走話題
Armed men tried to hijack the plane shortly after it took off.
(起飛後不久，武裝分子企圖劫持那架飛機。)
He always hijacks the conversation and talks only about himself.
(他總是搶走話題，只談論自己的事。)

hoarse(adj.)(聲音)沙啞的
hoarsely(adv.)沙啞地
go hoarse 嗓子變啞
hoarse voice 沙啞的聲音
After cheering for three hours at the game, my voice went hoarse.
(在比賽中加油三個小時後，我的聲音都啞了。)
The teacher spoke in a hoarse voice because she had a bad cold.
(老師因重感冒而聲音沙啞。)

homosexual(adj./n.)同性戀的、同性戀者
homosexuality(n.)同性戀
homosexual couple 同性伴侶
homosexual rights 同志權益
In 2019, Taiwan became the first place in Asia to legalize marriage for homosexual couples.
(2019 年，台灣成為亞洲第一個讓同性伴侶婚姻合法化的地方。)
The class discussed how attitudes toward homosexual people have changed over time.
(全班討論了社會對同性戀者的態度如何隨時間改變。)

honorary(adj.)榮譽的、名譽的
honor(n.)榮譽
honorary degree 榮譽學位
honorary citizen 榮譽市民
The university awarded the famous writer an honorary degree.
(那所大學頒給這位知名作家榮譽學位。)
The coach was made an honorary citizen of the city after the victory.
(那位教練在獲勝後被授予榮譽市民的身分。)

hospitable(adj.)好客的、宜人的
hospitality(n.)好客、款待
inhospitable(adj.)不好客的、荒涼的
hospitable people 好客的人們
be hospitable to 對…好客
The local people were so hospitable that we felt at home.
(當地人非常好客，讓我們感到賓至如歸。)
The warm climate makes the island hospitable to many kinds of plants.
(溫暖的氣候使這座島適合許多種植物生長。)

hospitality(n.)好客、殷勤款待、餐旅業
hospitable(adj.)好客的
warm hospitality 熱情款待
hospitality industry 餐旅業
Thank you for your warm hospitality during our stay in Tainan.
(謝謝你們在我們停留台南期間的熱情款待。)
She plans to study hospitality management and work in a hotel.
(她打算讀餐旅管理並在飯店工作。)

hospitalize(v.)使住院
hospital(n.)醫院
hospitalization(n.)住院
be hospitalized for 因…住院
hospitalized patients 住院病人
He was hospitalized for a week after the serious car accident.
(他在嚴重車禍後住院了一個星期。)
Several students were hospitalized after eating spoiled food at the camp.
(幾名學生在營隊吃了壞掉的食物後住院。)

hostel(n.)青年旅館、招待所
(無詞性變化)
youth hostel 青年旅館
stay at a hostel 住青年旅館
Backpackers often stay at youth hostels to save money.
(背包客常住青年旅館來省錢。)
The hostel near the station was clean, cheap, and full of travelers.
(車站附近的青年旅館乾淨、便宜，而且住滿了旅客。)

hover(v./n.)盤旋、徘徊、搖擺不定
(無詞性變化)
hover over 在…上空盤旋
hover around 在…左右徘徊
A helicopter hovered over the building during the rescue.
(救援期間，一架直升機在大樓上空盤旋。)
Temperatures hovered around 35 degrees for most of the week.
(這週大部分時間氣溫都在三十五度上下徘徊。)

humiliate(v.)羞辱、使丟臉
humiliation(n.)羞辱
humiliating(adj.)丟臉的、屈辱的
publicly humiliate 公開羞辱
feel humiliated 感到受辱
The coach humiliated the player by shouting at him in front of everyone.
(教練當眾對那名球員大吼，讓他顏面盡失。)
Losing the game 10 to 0 was a humiliating experience for the team.
(以十比零輸球對球隊來說是一次屈辱的經驗。)

hunch(n./v.)直覺、預感、弓起背
(無詞性變化)
have a hunch 有預感
hunch over 駝背、彎身
I have a hunch that our team is going to win today.
(我有預感我們隊今天會贏。)
Sitting hunched over a phone for hours is bad for your back.
(駝著背滑手機好幾個小時對背部不好。)

hurdle(n./v.)障礙、欄架、跨越障礙
hurdler(n.)跨欄選手
overcome a hurdle 克服障礙
clear a hurdle 跨過欄架
Passing the entrance exam was the first hurdle on his way to medical school.
(通過入學考試是他進入醫學院路上的第一道關卡。)
She won the gold medal in the 100-meter hurdles.
(她在一百公尺跨欄中奪得金牌。)

hybrid(adj./n.)混合的、雜交的、混種、混合物
hybridize(v.)使雜交
hybrid car 油電混合車
hybrid of 混合體
Hybrid cars use both gasoline and electricity to save energy.
(油電混合車同時使用汽油和電力來節省能源。)
The new course is a hybrid of online and classroom learning.
(這門新課程結合了線上學習與課堂學習。)

hygiene(n.)衛生、衛生學
hygienic(adj.)衛生的
personal hygiene 個人衛生
food hygiene 食品衛生
Washing your hands often is an important part of personal hygiene.
(經常洗手是個人衛生的重要一環。)
The restaurant was fined for poor food hygiene.
(那家餐廳因食品衛生不佳而被罰款。)

hypocrite(n.)偽君子、虛偽的人
hypocrisy(n.)虛偽
hypocritical(adj.)虛偽的
total hypocrite 十足的偽君子
call sb. a hypocrite 說某人虛偽
He tells others to save energy but drives everywhere, so people call him a hypocrite.
(他叫別人節能卻到哪都開車，所以大家說他是偽君子。)
I don't want to be a hypocrite who says one thing and does another.
(我不想當個說一套做一套的偽君子。)

iceberg(n.)冰山
(無詞性變化)
the tip of the iceberg 冰山一角
hit an iceberg 撞上冰山
The Titanic sank after it hit an iceberg in 1912.
(鐵達尼號在 1912 年撞上冰山後沉沒。)
The cases we know about are just the tip of the iceberg.
(我們所知道的案例只是冰山一角。)

illuminate(v.)照亮、闡明、啟發
illumination(n.)照明、闡明
illuminating(adj.)富啟發性的
brightly illuminated 燈火通明
illuminate the problem 闡明問題
At night, thousands of lights illuminate Taipei 101.
(夜晚，成千上萬盞燈照亮台北 101。)
The professor used simple examples to illuminate the difficult theory.
(教授用簡單的例子闡明那個艱澀的理論。)

imminent(adj.)即將發生的、迫近的
imminence(n.)迫近
imminent danger 迫在眉睫的危險
imminent threat 迫切的威脅
Dark clouds and strong winds warned us that a storm was imminent.
(烏雲和強風警告我們暴風雨即將來臨。)
The old bridge was closed because it was in imminent danger of collapse.
(那座舊橋因隨時可能倒塌而被封閉。)

imperative(adj./n.)極重要的、必要的、命令的、必要之事
(無詞性變化)
it is imperative that 務必…
moral imperative 道德義務
It is imperative that we take action to reduce plastic waste.
(我們務必採取行動減少塑膠垃圾。)
Protecting children's safety is a moral imperative for every society.
(保護兒童安全是每個社會的道德義務。)

imperial(adj.)帝國的、皇帝的
empire(n.)帝國
emperor(n.)皇帝
imperial palace 皇宮
imperial family 皇室
Tourists line up every day to visit the Imperial Palace in Tokyo.
(遊客每天排隊參觀東京的皇居。)
The museum displays treasures used by the imperial family of China.
(這間博物館展出中國皇室使用過的寶物。)

implicit(adj.)含蓄的、暗示的、絕對的
implicitly(adv.)含蓄地、絕對地
implicit meaning 言外之意
implicit trust 絕對信任
There was an implicit criticism in his polite comment.
(他那句客氣的評論中隱含著批評。)
The team has implicit trust in their captain's decisions.
(隊員們絕對信任隊長的決定。)

imposing(adj.)壯觀的、雄偉的、氣勢逼人的
impose(v.)強加
imposing building 雄偉的建築
imposing figure 威風凜凜的人物
The Presidential Office is an imposing building in central Taipei.
(總統府是台北市中心一座雄偉的建築。)
The tall, serious principal was an imposing figure to new students.
(那位高大嚴肅的校長對新生來說很有威嚴。)

imprison(v.)監禁、使入獄、imprisonment(n.)監禁、徒刑
prison(n.)監獄
life imprisonment 無期徒刑
be imprisoned for 因…入獄
The man was imprisoned for ten years for robbing a bank.
(那名男子因搶劫銀行被判入獄十年。)
The judge sentenced the killer to life imprisonment.
(法官判處那名兇手無期徒刑。)

incline(v./n.)傾向於、使傾斜、斜坡
inclination(n.)傾向、意願
inclined(adj.)傾向於…的
be inclined to 傾向於
steep incline 陡坡
I am inclined to agree with you, but I need more information.
(我傾向於同意你，但我需要更多資訊。)
The bikers slowed down as they rode up the steep incline.
(自行車騎士騎上陡坡時放慢了速度。)

inclusive(adj.)包含在內的、包容的
include(v.)包含
inclusion(n.)包含、融合
inclusive education 融合教育
all-inclusive 費用全包的
The school promotes inclusive education for students of all abilities.
(這所學校推動讓各種能力的學生一起學習的融合教育。)
We booked an all-inclusive trip, so meals and tickets are already paid for.
(我們訂了全包式旅遊，所以餐點和門票都已付清。)

incur(v.)招致、引起、蒙受
(無詞性變化)
incur costs 產生費用
incur anger 招致憤怒
You will incur a late fee if you return the book after the due date.
(如果在到期日後還書，你將被收取逾期費。)
The new policy incurred the anger of many local residents.
(新政策引起許多當地居民的憤怒。)

indifference(n.)冷漠、漠不關心
indifferent(adj.)漠不關心的
indifferently(adv.)冷漠地
indifference to 對…的冷漠
with indifference 冷淡地
Many people showed indifference to the problem of climate change.
(許多人對氣候變遷問題漠不關心。)
She listened to his excuses with complete indifference.
(她完全冷淡地聽著他的藉口。)

indignant(adj.)憤慨的、義憤的
indignation(n.)憤慨
indignantly(adv.)憤慨地
indignant at 對…感到憤慨
indignant protest 憤慨的抗議
The customers were indignant at being treated so rudely by the staff.
(顧客對於遭到店員如此無禮的對待感到憤慨。)
'I did not cheat!' the student replied indignantly.
(「我沒有作弊！」那個學生憤慨地回答。)

induce(v.)誘使、引起、導致
inducement(n.)誘因
induction(n.)歸納法、就職
induce sb. to 誘使某人
induce sleep 誘發睡意
Nothing could induce him to change his mind about the plan.
(沒有任何事能讓他改變對這個計畫的想法。)
Some medicines may induce sleep, so don't drive after taking them.
(有些藥物會引起睡意，所以服用後別開車。)

industrialize(v.)使工業化
industrial(adj.)工業的
industrialization(n.)工業化
rapidly industrialize 快速工業化
industrialized countries 工業化國家
Taiwan industrialized rapidly in the second half of the twentieth century.
(台灣在二十世紀下半葉迅速工業化。)
Industrialized countries produce much more carbon dioxide than poor nations.
(工業化國家排放的二氧化碳遠多於貧窮國家。)

infectious(adj.)傳染性的、有感染力的
infect(v.)傳染
infection(n.)感染
infectious disease 傳染病
infectious laugh 有感染力的笑聲
Doctors are working hard to stop the spread of infectious diseases.
(醫生們正努力阻止傳染病的擴散。)
Her infectious laugh made everyone in the room smile.
(她富有感染力的笑聲讓房裡每個人都笑了。)

infer(v.)推論、推斷
inference(n.)推論
infer from 從…推斷
make an inference 做出推論
From his silence, I inferred that he was not happy with the result.
(從他的沉默中，我推斷他對結果並不滿意。)
Readers can infer the main idea from the first paragraph.
(讀者可以從第一段推論出主旨。)

inflict(v.)施加(打擊、傷害等)、使承受
infliction(n.)施加、痛苦
inflict damage 造成損害
inflict pain on 使…承受痛苦
The typhoon inflicted serious damage on farms in southern Taiwan.
(颱風對南台灣的農田造成嚴重損害。)
Bullies often inflict pain on others to feel powerful.
(霸凌者常藉由使他人痛苦來感覺自己強大。)

inhabit(v.)居住於、棲息於
inhabitant(n.)居民
habitat(n.)棲息地
inhabit an area 居住在某地區
densely inhabited 人口稠密的
Many rare birds inhabit the wetlands along the west coast.
(許多稀有鳥類棲息在西海岸的濕地。)
The island was once inhabited by only a few fishing families.
(這座島曾經只有少數幾戶漁民居住。)

inhabitant(n.)居民、棲息的動物
inhabit(v.)居住於
local inhabitants 當地居民
original inhabitants 原住民、原始居民
The town has about five thousand inhabitants, most of whom are farmers.
(這個鎮大約有五千名居民，其中大多數是農民。)
The original inhabitants of the island had their own language and culture.
(這座島的原始居民有自己的語言和文化。)

injustice(n.)不公正、不公平的事
justice(n.)正義
unjust(adj.)不公正的
social injustice 社會不公
fight injustice 對抗不公
Many young people joined the protest to fight social injustice.
(許多年輕人參加抗議活動來對抗社會不公。)
He felt a deep sense of injustice when he was punished for something he didn't do.
(他因沒做過的事受罰時，深感不公平。)

inland(adj./adv./n.)內陸的、在內陸、內陸地區
(無詞性變化)
inland areas 內陸地區
move inland 向內陸移動
The typhoon weakened as it moved inland over the mountains.
(颱風向內陸移動越過山脈後減弱了。)
Inland areas usually have hotter summers than coastal cities.
(內陸地區的夏天通常比沿海城市炎熱。)

innumerable(adj.)無數的、數不清的
numerous(adj.)眾多的
innumerable stars 無數的星星
innumerable times 無數次
On a clear night in the mountains, you can see innumerable stars.
(在山上晴朗的夜晚，你可以看到無數的星星。)
The scientist repeated the experiment innumerable times before she succeeded.
(那位科學家重複實驗了無數次才成功。)

inquire(v.)詢問、打聽、調查
inquiry(n.)詢問、調查
inquire about 詢問有關…
inquire into 調查
I called the hotel to inquire about room prices for next weekend.
(我打電話到飯店詢問下週末的房價。)
The committee will inquire into the causes of the accident.
(委員會將調查這起意外的原因。)

insistence(n.)堅持、強調
insist(v.)堅持
insistent(adj.)堅持的
at sb.'s insistence 在某人的堅持下
insistence on 堅持…
At my mother's insistence, I wore a jacket even though it was warm.
(在媽媽的堅持下，雖然天氣暖和我還是穿了外套。)
His insistence on doing everything by himself slowed the whole team down.
(他堅持凡事親力親為，拖慢了整個團隊。)

instinctive(adj.)本能的、直覺的
instinct(n.)本能
instinctively(adv.)本能地
instinctive reaction 本能反應
instinctive fear 本能的恐懼
Pulling your hand away from something hot is an instinctive reaction.
(碰到燙的東西時把手縮回是一種本能反應。)
She instinctively covered her head when the shelf began to fall.
(架子開始倒下時，她本能地護住頭部。)

intake(n.)攝取量、吸入、招收人數
(無詞性變化)
calorie intake 卡路里攝取量
sugar intake 糖分攝取
Doctors advise people to reduce their daily sugar intake.
(醫生建議人們減少每天的糖分攝取。)
The school plans to increase its student intake next year.
(這所學校計畫明年增加招生人數。)

intellect(n.)智力、才智、知識分子
intellectual(adj./n.)智力的、知識分子
intelligent(adj.)聰明的
sharp intellect 敏銳的才智
a person of great intellect 才智過人的人
Einstein was a man of great intellect and imagination.
(愛因斯坦是一位才智與想像力兼具的人。)
Reading widely helps develop both your intellect and your character.
(廣泛閱讀有助於培養你的才智與品格。)

interpreter(n.)口譯員、詮釋者
interpret(v.)口譯、詮釋
interpretation(n.)解釋、口譯
sign language interpreter 手語翻譯員
through an interpreter 透過口譯員
The president spoke to the foreign guests through an interpreter.
(總統透過口譯員與外賓交談。)
A sign language interpreter stood beside the speaker during the press conference.
(記者會期間，一位手語翻譯員站在發言人身旁。)

intersection(n.)十字路口、交叉點
intersect(v.)相交、交叉
busy intersection 繁忙的十字路口
at the intersection 在十字路口
Turn left at the next intersection, and you will see the museum.
(在下一個路口左轉，你就會看到博物館。)
Two cars crashed at the busy intersection near our school.
(兩輛車在我們學校附近繁忙的十字路口相撞。)

intervene(v.)干預、介入、調停
intervention(n.)干預、介入
intervene in 介入…
intervene between 在…之間調停
The teacher had to intervene when the two students started fighting.
(那兩名學生開始打架時，老師不得不介入。)
The government decided not to intervene in the price war.
(政府決定不介入這場價格戰。)

intimacy(n.)親密、親近
intimate(adj.)親密的
emotional intimacy 情感上的親密
a sense of intimacy 親密感
The small café has a warm sense of intimacy that customers love.
(這家小咖啡館有一種顧客喜愛的溫馨親密感。)
Sharing secrets can build intimacy between close friends.
(分享秘密能拉近好朋友之間的距離。)

intimidate(v.)恐嚇、威脅、使膽怯
intimidation(n.)恐嚇
intimidating(adj.)令人生畏的
feel intimidated 感到膽怯
intimidate witnesses 恐嚇證人
Don't let the size of the other team intimidate you.
(別讓對手的體型嚇倒你。)
Speaking in front of the whole school can be intimidating at first.
(一開始在全校面前說話可能會讓人膽怯。)

intonation(n.)語調、聲調
intone(v.)吟誦
rising intonation 上揚的語調
falling intonation 下降的語調
In English, yes-no questions usually end with a rising intonation.
(在英文中，是非問句通常以上揚語調結尾。)
Her intonation made it clear that she was joking.
(從她的語調明顯聽得出來她在開玩笑。)

intrigue(n./v.)陰謀、詭計、激起興趣
intriguing(adj.)引人入勝的
political intrigue 政治陰謀
be intrigued by 對…很感興趣
The novel is full of political intrigue and surprising twists.
(這本小說充滿了政治陰謀和出人意料的轉折。)
I was intrigued by the strange symbols carved on the old stone.
(我對那塊古老石頭上刻的奇怪符號很感興趣。)

intrude(v.)闖入、侵入、打擾
intruder(n.)入侵者
intrusion(n.)侵擾
intrude on 打擾、侵犯
intrude into 闖入
I'm sorry to intrude, but there is an urgent call for you.
(抱歉打擾，但有一通找你的緊急電話。)
Reporters should not intrude on people's private lives.
(記者不應侵犯他人的私生活。)

intruder(n.)入侵者、闖入者
intrude(v.)闖入
intrusion(n.)侵入
armed intruder 武裝入侵者
catch an intruder 抓到闖入者
The alarm went off when an intruder broke into the house at midnight.
(半夜有人闖入屋內時，警報器響了起來。)
The dog barked loudly to warn its owner of the intruder.
(那隻狗大聲吠叫，警告主人有人闖入。)

invaluable(adj.)無價的、極寶貴的
value(n.)價值
valuable(adj.)有價值的
invaluable experience 寶貴的經驗
invaluable help 極大的幫助
Working as a volunteer gave me invaluable experience in dealing with people.
(擔任志工讓我在與人相處方面獲得寶貴的經驗。)
Your advice has been invaluable to me during this difficult time.
(在這段艱難時期，你的建議對我來說非常寶貴。)

invariably(adv.)總是、一向
invariable(adj.)不變的
almost invariably 幾乎總是
invariably late 總是遲到
When he is nervous, he invariably starts talking too fast.
(他一緊張，總是會開始講太快。)
Our weekend plans are invariably canceled because of the rain.
(我們的週末計畫總是因下雨而取消。)

inventory(n./v.)存貨、清單、盤點
(無詞性變化)
take inventory 盤點存貨
inventory list 存貨清單
The store closes early once a month to take inventory.
(這家店每個月提早關門一次以盤點存貨。)
The manager made a detailed inventory of all the computers in the office.
(經理把辦公室裡所有電腦列出一份詳細的清單。)

ironic(adj.)諷刺的、反諷的
irony(n.)諷刺
ironically(adv.)諷刺地
it is ironic that 諷刺的是
ironic smile 嘲諷的微笑
It is ironic that the fire station itself burned down.
(諷刺的是，消防局本身竟然燒毀了。)
Ironically, the health expert was the first to catch the flu.
(諷刺的是，那位健康專家是第一個得流感的。)

irritable(adj.)易怒的、急躁的
irritate(v.)激怒
irritability(n.)易怒
become irritable 變得煩躁
irritable mood 煩躁的心情
Lack of sleep can make people irritable and less focused.
(睡眠不足會讓人變得易怒且不專心。)
He gets irritable when he is hungry, so we always bring snacks.
(他一餓就會變得暴躁，所以我們總會帶點零食。)

irritate(v.)激怒、使惱怒、刺激(皮膚等)
irritation(n.)惱怒、刺激
irritating(adj.)令人惱火的
irritate the skin 刺激皮膚
be irritated by 對…感到惱怒
Her habit of interrupting others really irritates me.
(她打斷別人說話的習慣真的讓我很惱火。)
Some soaps contain chemicals that may irritate sensitive skin.
(有些肥皂含有可能刺激敏感肌膚的化學物質。)

isle(n.)島、小島
islet(n.)小島
the British Isles 英倫諸島
tropical isle 熱帶小島
They spent their honeymoon on a quiet tropical isle.
(他們在一座寧靜的熱帶小島上度蜜月。)
The British Isles include Great Britain, Ireland, and many smaller islands.
(英倫諸島包括大不列顛島、愛爾蘭島以及許多小島。)

itch(n./v.)癢、渴望、發癢
itchy(adj.)發癢的
have an itch 發癢
itch to 渴望做…
Mosquito bites made my arms itch all night.
(蚊子叮咬讓我的手臂癢了一整晚。)
After months of studying, I'm itching to go on a trip.
(讀了幾個月的書後，我很想去旅行。)

ivy(n.)常春藤
(無詞性變化)
covered in ivy 爬滿常春藤
Ivy League 常春藤聯盟
The walls of the old library are covered in green ivy.
(那座老圖書館的牆上爬滿了綠色的常春藤。)
She hopes to study at an Ivy League university in the United States.
(她希望能就讀美國的常春藤聯盟大學。)

jade(n.)玉、翡翠
(無詞性變化)
jade bracelet 玉鐲
jade market 玉市
My grandmother gave me a jade bracelet as a birthday gift.
(奶奶送我一只玉鐲當作生日禮物。)
The Jadeite Cabbage is one of the most famous treasures in the National Palace Museum.
(翠玉白菜是故宮博物院最著名的館藏之一。)

janitor(n.)工友、管理員
(無詞性變化)
school janitor 學校工友
work as a janitor 擔任管理員
The school janitor fixed the broken window in our classroom.
(學校工友修好了我們教室破掉的窗戶。)
He worked as a janitor at night to pay for his college education.
(他晚上當清潔管理員來支付大學學費。)

jasmine(n.)茉莉、茉莉花
(無詞性變化)
jasmine tea 茉莉花茶
jasmine flowers 茉莉花
The sweet smell of jasmine filled the garden in the evening.
(傍晚時，茉莉花的香甜氣味瀰漫整座花園。)
My mother likes to drink a cup of jasmine tea after dinner.
(我媽媽喜歡在晚餐後喝一杯茉莉花茶。)

jingle(n./v.)叮噹聲、廣告歌曲、發出叮噹聲
(無詞性變化)
jingle bells 叮噹鈴
advertising jingle 廣告歌曲
The keys in his pocket jingled as he walked down the hall.
(他走過走廊時，口袋裡的鑰匙叮噹作響。)
That catchy advertising jingle has been stuck in my head all day.
(那首朗朗上口的廣告歌一整天都在我腦中揮之不去。)

jockey(n./v.)賽馬騎師、操作者、謀取(地位)
(無詞性變化)
disc jockey 電台或舞會的音樂主持人(DJ)
jockey for position 爭奪有利位置
The jockey guided his horse to victory in the final race.
(那位騎師在最後一場比賽中策馬奪冠。)
Several companies are jockeying for position in the electric car market.
(好幾家公司正在電動車市場中爭奪有利地位。)

jolly(adj./adv./v./n.)愉快的、非常、哄騙、歡樂
jollity(n.)歡樂
jolly good 非常好
jolly old man 快活的老人
Santa Claus is often described as a jolly old man with a white beard.
(聖誕老人常被描述成一位留著白鬍子的快活老人。)
We had a jolly time singing songs around the campfire.
(我們圍著營火唱歌，度過了歡樂的時光。)

joyous(adj.)充滿歡樂的、快樂的
joy(n.)歡樂
joyously(adv.)快樂地
joyous occasion 喜慶的場合
joyous celebration 歡慶
The wedding was a joyous occasion for both families.
(這場婚禮對兩家人來說都是喜慶的場合。)
Crowds filled the streets for a joyous celebration after the team's victory.
(球隊獲勝後，人群湧上街頭歡慶。)

junction(n.)交叉點、交流道、匯合處
join(v.)連接
railway junction 鐵路樞紐
highway junction 交流道
Take the highway and exit at the next junction for Hsinchu.
(上高速公路後，在下一個交流道下往新竹。)
The town grew quickly because it was an important railway junction.
(這個鎮因為是重要的鐵路樞紐而迅速發展。)

kin(n./adj.)親屬、家族、有親屬關係的
kinship(n.)親屬關係
next of kin 最近親屬
kith and kin 親朋好友
The hospital contacted the patient's next of kin after the accident.
(意外發生後，醫院聯絡了病人的最近親屬。)
During the Lunar New Year, many people return home to visit their kin.
(農曆新年期間，許多人返鄉探望親人。)

kindle(v.)點燃、激起
kindling(n.)引火物
kindle a fire 生火
kindle interest 激起興趣
We used dry leaves and small sticks to kindle a fire at the campsite.
(我們在營地用乾葉子和小樹枝生火。)
A trip to the science museum kindled his interest in space.
(一趟科學博物館之旅激起了他對太空的興趣。)

knowledgeable(adj.)知識淵博的、有見識的
knowledge(n.)知識
knowledgeably(adv.)有見識地
knowledgeable about 對…很了解
knowledgeable staff 專業的工作人員
Our history teacher is very knowledgeable about ancient Chinese culture.
(我們的歷史老師對中國古代文化非常了解。)
The museum guide was friendly and knowledgeable, answering all our questions.
(博物館導覽員親切又博學，回答了我們所有的問題。)
